title: Pivot Report in Jira Assistant
content:
The Pivot Report in Jira Assistant (JA) lets you design your own reports from Jira issues without writing code. Choose the issues using a JQL query or the sprints of agile boards, drag the fields you need into the report and decide which become rows and which become columns. The report groups, counts, sums, averages and formats the values and shows the result as a table.
Open it from the menu Reports > Pivot Report. It opens the Pivot Report home, which lists your saved reports and the sample reports. Use 'Create report' to start an empty report, open a sample to start from a ready-made report, or open one of your reports from its card.
Examples: number of issues by status and issue type, time logged by each user per day of a week, story points committed and completed by sprint or epic, open issues by age, issue lists grouped by project or fix version with totals.
Quick start: create a report (the Report Config panel opens on the right with the data source), choose JQL query or Sprints, drag fields such as Status and Assignee into the Report Fields area, click a field to open its properties and turn on 'Show values of this field as columns (pivot)' on the field that should become columns, drag value fields such as Story Points (Sum) under it, then click the play icon to generate or the save icon to save.
Works with Jira Cloud and Jira Data Center / Server.

title: Pivot Report home and sample reports in Jira Assistant
content:
The Pivot Report home in Jira Assistant (JA) opens from Reports > Pivot Report. It shows 'My reports' with your saved reports and a gallery of sample reports grouped by category, such as sprints, issues, time tracking and releases.
Samples work with any Jira. They ask for the projects, boards or period while generating the report. Opening a sample previews it straight away with a banner saying it is a sample. You can open the Report Config panel and change the sample like any report, e.g. edit its JQL, add fields or change the date range, and generate it again.
Click 'Save as my report' in the banner to keep the sample, with your changes, as your own report. A sample is saved as your own report only when you save it; until then the sample itself stays unchanged. The back button of the banner returns to the home.

title: Asking for values while generating a Pivot Report (report parameters)
content:
A Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report can ask for values each time it is generated instead of fixing them in the report:
JQL: use parameters('Name') in the JQL of the data source, e.g. project = parameters('Project').
Filters: use parameters('Name') in a field filter, e.g. issuetype = parameters('Type').
Date Range field: set Dates to 'Ask while generating' and give the parameter a name; the same name used in the JQL, e.g. worklogDate >= startDate(parameters('Period')), pulls only the issues of those dates. 'Fixed dates' keeps the dates in the report.
Sprints: turn on 'Choose sprints while generating the report' in the data source. The report then asks for the agile boards and sprints under 'Boards and sprints', starting with the default range chosen for each board, such as the last 2 sprints.
A parameter used in several places is asked only once. Saved reports ask for their values again when opened, and the list icon in the report header changes them later.

title: Choosing the issues for a Pivot Report (JQL or sprints)
content:
The data source of a Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report decides which issues are pulled from Jira. It is shown when a new report is created and can be opened again using the back arrow (Configure data source) icon in the Report Config panel. Under 'Pull issues using' choose:
JQL query: all the issues matching the query are pulled.
Sprints: choose one or more agile boards and then the sprints of each board. Pick a range of recent sprints (Last sprint, Last closed sprint, Last 2 to 5 sprints) or choose specific sprints. A JQL query can be added to narrow the issues of the selected sprints further.
To switch to other sprints, open the Report Config panel using the edit icon, change the sprints and refresh the report. Relative choices such as 'Last sprint' move to the new sprint automatically once it starts.
Tip: keep filters that apply to the whole report in the JQL itself, so only the needed issues are pulled and the report stays fast; use field filters only to refine groups.

title: Fields list in the Jira Assistant Pivot Report
content:
The fields list on the right of the Pivot Report's Report Config panel in Jira Assistant (JA) shows all the fields of Jira in three sections with the number of fields in each:
Native: fields provided by Jira, such as Status, Assignee, Created, Time Spent and Sprint.
Custom: custom fields of your Jira instance, such as Story Points or Team.
Derived: properties of the items within an issue, such as Worklog Added By, Worklog Time spent, Comment Added Time, Attachment File Name, Component Name and Fix Version Release Date, and the special Date Range field.
Use the search box to find a field by name or key. The icon in front of each field shows its type. The copy icon copies the name of the field in the form used in filters (names with spaces are wrapped in backticks). Drag a field into the Report Fields area to add it. The same field can be added more than once, e.g. to show both the sum and the average.

title: Row fields and grouping in the Pivot Report
content:
The Report Fields area of the Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report lists the fields used in the report in the order they are shown. Drag them by the grip handle to reorder and use the cross icon to remove. Each field shows a summary of its configuration (Grouped, Pivot, List or the aggregation function) and a filter icon when a filter is applied. Click a field to open its Field Properties at the bottom of the panel; the divider can be dragged to resize it.
By default every field is a row field and each issue is shown as a separate row. 'Group the issues by this field' combines the issues having the same value into one row; group by more than one field for nested groups. Fields after a grouped field show the combined value of the issues of the group using the aggregation function. Choose 'No Aggregation' to keep one row per issue within the group.

title: Column groups (pivot) in the Pivot Report
content:
In the Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report, turn on 'Show values of this field as columns (pivot)' in the properties of a field to show each value of the field as a column, e.g. one column per status.
A column group needs at least one field under it: drag fields from the fields list and drop them under the column group. A field under it with 'Group the issues by this field' becomes a nested column group. A field that is not grouped becomes a value shown in the cells, combined using its aggregation function, e.g. Count of Key or Sum of Story Points.
'Show total column' adds a total for the group, shown at start or at end.

title: Aggregation functions and display formats in the Pivot Report
content:
Header text: text shown in the column header of a Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report field. When empty, the name of the field is used, with the aggregation function when used, e.g. 'Story Points (Sum)'.
Aggregation function: how the values of all the issues of a group are combined into one cell. Only functions suitable for the type of the field are listed: First value (default, all fields), Last value (all fields), Count (all fields, with 'Count distinct values only' to count each value once), Sum and Avg (number and time spent fields), Min and Max (number, time spent, date and date time fields), Merge (CSV) (text fields, values separated by commas), No Aggregation (row fields only, one row per issue within the group).
Display format: Date and date time - Default, Date only, Age in days (words) or Age in days (number). User - name, email or both, with or without avatar. Time spent - formatted or as a number. Project - key, name or both. Parent - key, summary or both, with or without status.
Filter issues: available for grouped fields and column groups; only the issues matching the filter are included under the field.

title: Date Range field (timesheet columns) in the Pivot Report
content:
The Date Range field in the Derived section of the Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report creates one column for each day or week of a period, useful for timesheets. It can be used only as a column group.
Date range: the period for which the columns are created. Show columns as: Days grouped by week, or Weeks grouped by month. Date field to match: the date field that decides under which date an issue is shown; use a derived date field such as Worklog Time to place each worklog under its own date. Add the values to show under it, e.g. Worklog Time spent with Sum.

title: Filters and filter validation in the Pivot Report
content:
Filters in the Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report are SQL-like expressions written in the filter box of a grouped field or column group. They are validated as you type: an error is shown below the filter box, or 'Filter is valid' when it is correct. Validation is case-insensitive and rejects unknown fields, unknown functions and incompatible comparisons. Reports with invalid filters are not generated and the errors are listed instead.
Field names: native fields are referred by their key, e.g. status, assignee, created or timespent. Custom fields are referred by their name or id, e.g. `Story Points` or customfield_10016; names having spaces must be wrapped in backticks. Derived fields are referred by their path, e.g. worklog.author, worklog.timeSpentSeconds, comment.created or fixVersions.name. The copy icon next to a field in the fields list copies its name in the right form.
Combine conditions using 'and' and 'or', and use brackets to group them, e.g. (status = 'Open' or status = 'Reopened') and priority in ('High', 'Highest').
Values can be compared only with values of a compatible type, e.g. a date field with a date. The range operators (>, <, >=, <=, between) can be used only with number, date and time spent fields.
The like operator uses % as the wildcard and the text must have at least three characters other than the wildcards.

title: Comparison operators in Pivot Report filters
content:
Filters in the Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report support SQL-like comparison operators, similar to a WHERE clause.
= (equal) and != (not equal): e.g. Priority = 'High', Status != 'Closed'. The <> operator is not supported; use != instead.
in: value in a list, e.g. Assignee in ('User1','User2').
between: range for number, date or time spent fields, e.g. DueDate between '2023-01-01' and '2023-03-31'.
>, <, >=, <=: threshold comparisons for number, date or time spent fields, e.g. StoryPoints > 5, Created < '2023-06-01', DueDate >= '2023-09-01', ResolutionDate <= '2023-08-15'.
like: substring match on text fields using % as the wildcard, with at least three characters other than wildcards, e.g. Summary like '%bug%'.

title: Pivot Report filter functions overview and parameters()
content:
The Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report filters support functions in addition to the comparison operators: parameters, sum, avg, min, max, first, last, as_date, today, eod, startOfDay, now, date_diff, startDate, endDate and currentUser. Functions can be used with any field whose Jira field type suits the function and can be combined into SQL-like filter expressions. Any other function name is rejected by the filter validation.
currentUser() returns the logged-in user, e.g. assignee = currentUser().
parameters(paramName: string): any makes a report dynamic by asking for a value every time the report is generated, so filters need not be edited each run. No separate parameter creation is needed: the type of the parameter (date range, date, list or text) is decided by where it is used. The name must have 3 to 25 characters; using the same name in more than one place asks for the value only once. Example: assignee = parameters("Assignee list") or worklog.author in (parameters("User List")).
parameters() can also be used in the JQL of the data source, e.g. project = parameters('Project') or worklogDate >= startDate(parameters('Period')), so only the issues matching the value are pulled from Jira.
Values are asked under 'Values asked while generating the report' before the report is generated; click 'Generate report' after providing them. The list icon in the report header changes the values later.

title: Aggregate functions in Pivot Report filters
content:
The Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report filters provide aggregate functions over arrays of values.
sum(values: array of number | timespent): number | timespent returns the total, e.g. timespent > sum(worklog.timeSpentSeconds).
avg(values: array of number | timespent): number | timespent returns the average, e.g. avg(worklog.timeSpentSeconds) > 3600.
min(values: array of number | timespent | date | datetime) returns the smallest value of the same type, e.g. min(dueDate) > startDate(parameters("Due date range")).
max(values: array of number | timespent | date | datetime) returns the largest value of the same type, e.g. max(dueDate) < endDate(parameters("Due date range")).
first(values: array of any): any and last(values: array of any): any return the first and last element of an array, e.g. first(key), last(key).

title: Date and time functions in Pivot Report filters
content:
The Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report filters include date/time helper functions. The optional offset of today, eod, startOfDay and now is either a number of days (e.g. -7) or a sign followed by an amount and a unit (e.g. "-10d"). Units: y (years), Q (quarters), M (months), w (weeks), d (days), h (hours), m (minutes).
today(value?: number | string): datetime returns the start of the current day, optionally moved, e.g. created >= today("-10d") or created >= today("-2w").
eod(value?: number | string): datetime returns the end of the current day, optionally moved, e.g. created <= eod("-10d") or dueDate <= eod("+2w"). There is no todayEOD function; use eod.
startOfDay(value?: number | string): datetime is the same as today, e.g. updated >= startOfDay("-1w").
now(value?: number | string): datetime returns the current date and time, optionally moved, e.g. dueDate between today("-10d") and now("+1w") or updated >= now("-4h").
as_date(value: number | date | datetime | string, format?: string) converts a value to a date using the optional format, e.g. dueDate >= as_date("10/15/2023", "MM/DD/YYYY").
date_diff(date1: datetime, date2: datetime, unit?: string): number returns date1 minus date2 in the given unit (default milliseconds). Units: years, months, weeks, days, hours, minutes or y, M, w, d, h, m. E.g. date_diff(min(worklog.created), created, "d") > 5 or date_diff(now(), updated, "days") > 30.
startDate(date: daterange): date and endDate(date: daterange): date extract the start and end of a date range parameter, e.g. created between startDate(parameters("Created between")) and endDate(parameters("Created between")).

title: Saving, reopening and sharing Pivot Reports in Jira Assistant
content:
In the Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report, the play icon in the Report Config panel generates the report and the refresh icon in the report header pulls the latest data from Jira. The save icon saves the report, the copy icon renames it or saves it as a new report and the trash icon deletes it. The edit icon in the report header shows or hides the Report Config panel.
Saved reports open from the Pivot Report home, from the report list in the report header, from the 'My Reports' gadget on the dashboard, or from a bookmarked address of the report. A saved report is generated as soon as it opens, with the Report Config panel hidden; if it asks for values, they are asked first. Once you have six or more reports, a search box on the home finds a report by its name.
Export the generated report from the gadget options menu in the report header as Excel, CSV or PDF.
To share reports, select them in the 'My Reports' gadget and export them as a .jrd file. Others can import the file using the import option of the same gadget, and can rename each report before importing it.
Errors in the report definition, such as a column group without values or an invalid filter, are listed when the report is generated.

title: Pivot Report tips and limitations
content:
Fields with more than one value in the Jira Assistant (JA) Pivot Report, such as Labels, Components, Sprint or worklogs, place the issue under each of its values, e.g. an issue that was part of two sprints is counted under both sprints.
Groups are shown in the order in which their values are first found. A cell with no matching issues is shown empty.
For best performance, restrict the issues in the JQL or by choosing only the needed sprints, then refine further with filters.
The Pivot Report works with Jira Cloud and Jira Data Center / Server.

title: Custom Report module in Jira Assistant
content:
The Custom Report module in Jira Assistant (JA) lets you generate a simple report by filtering data with JQL and choosing which columns to display.
You can format the displayed data using predefined formats and group the results by one or more columns.
Once saved, a Custom Report appears in the 'My Reports' gadget and the add-gadget popup, so it can be added to a dashboard as a gadget.

title: Using expressions in the Custom Report
content:
Expressions in the Jira Assistant (JA) Custom Report are essentially JavaScript code, with the current row's data available in a Field object.
You can use most built-in JavaScript functions and operators, for example Field.assignee.name, Field.summary, parseInt(Field.timespent), and the JavaScript Math class for calculations.
This lets you derive and format columns flexibly within Jira Assistant reports.

title: Building your own gadget with reports in Jira Assistant
content:
In Jira Assistant (JA) you can build your own dashboard gadget by creating a report with the Pivot Report or the Report Builder.
After saving the report, it becomes available in the 'Add a Gadget' list of the dashboard, where you can add it to any dashboard. A Report Builder gadget asks for the report parameters once and remembers them, and has buttons to change the parameters, print, export as PDF and open the report in the Report Builder.
This is the recommended way to get customized data views in Jira Assistant beyond what the inbuilt gadgets offer.

title: Showing specific Jira fields in Jira Assistant reports and gadgets
content:
Whether you can show specific Jira fields depends on the report or gadget in Jira Assistant (JA): some support choosing fields, while others show a fixed default set of fields.
The Worklog Report lets you select multiple native or custom fields as additional columns shown alongside the ticket details, from the 'Field list' tab of its settings.
The Pivot Report and Custom Report can use any Jira field to build the report you need. When asking about fields, specify which report or gadget you want them in.
